articles.headline: Commanders' Jayden Daniels-themed post aimed at Bengals tops NFL Week 11 trolls
articles.description: NFL teams remained petty in Week 11, led by a post from the Washington Commanders.
articles.body:
The unlikeliest of victories can often feel the sweetest -- especially when it can be capped with a troll.

The Washington Commanders beat the Cincinnati Bengals 22-20 on "Monday Night Football." Washington faced a one-point deficit with 46 seconds left after Cincinnati kicked a go-ahead field goal. The Commanders, though, had the last laugh.

Quarterback Jayden Daniels connected with wide receiver Antonio Williams twice during the final drive, including a 42-yard reception that set up a field goal. Drew Stevens nailed the 26-yarder as time expired, ensuring Washington's victory.

The Commanders poked fun at the Bengals on social media in clever fashion.

They posted a clip from a 2001 episode of the talk show "Maury," during which someone on the show shares their phobia of aluminum foil. While on stage, someone walks toward them with aluminum foil, prompting them to run off stage and yell, "Get away from me." Washington put its spin on the video, editing the host Maury Povich as "Monday Night Football," the lady with the aluminum foil fear as the Bengals and the aluminum foil as Daniels, who is 2-0 against the Bengals on "Monday Night Football."

Here are the top trolls from the NFL's Week 11.

Buffalo Bills 26, Miami Dolphins 9

Grand Theft Auto VI has taken over the entertainment world since its release Thursday. The video game's reach also carried over to the NFL, becoming the theme of a petty post Sunday.

The Buffalo Bills defeated the Miami Dolphins led by its defense. Buffalo gave up only 185 yards and picked off Dolphins quarterback Kyle McCord once. Josh Allen had two interceptions himself, but he also threw for 304 yards and a score.

Other teams such as the New York Jets and Chicago Bears tapped into the GTA VI space, but the Bills' attempt felt more direct as they faced the Dolphins. The victory prompted Buffalo to post a custom game cover inspired by that of GTA VI, which is set in "Vice City," a fictional version of Miami. Instead of it reading "GTA VI" across the cover, the Bills added: "Bills Win" with players scattered throughout it.

Carolina Panthers 35, Baltimore Ravens 33

It required a late stop, but the Carolina Panthers pulled out a wild victory against the Baltimore Ravens.

Carolina went ahead on a 37-yard field goal with 1:44 left. Baltimore received possession with a chance to go ahead before Jacoby Brissett was picked off with 36 seconds left, clinching the Panthers' win.

A clever caption kicked off Carolina's trolling as it wrote: "Came down to the wire," with "the wire" being a reference to the iconic HBO show set in Baltimore. Then, the Panthers shared a graphic of a panther standing over a Ravens helmet with the caption: "Charming," a reference to Baltimore's nickname as the "Charm City." They also wrote "nevermore" on the bottom in a nod to Edgar Allen Poe's "The Raven" poem where the raven featured repeats: "nevermore."

articles.headline: Commanders building momentum, halt Bengals' 5-game win streak
articles.description: The Commanders' defense held the potent Bengals in check and Washington has won three of four.
articles.body:
LANDOVER, Md. -- The Washington Commanders needed a win to keep pace in the NFC East. They not only got a win, their defense made a statement.

The Commanders upset the Cincinnati Bengals 22-20 on a last-second 28-yard field goal by Drew Stevens to win their second game in a row and third in their last four. It's the first time they've won consecutive games since the 2024 season.

Quarterback Jayden Daniels needed only two passes -- 23 yards and 42 yards into tight windows -- to lead the Commanders into field goal position. They improved to 4-5-1. A loss would have dropped them three games behind the first-place New York Giants in the NFC East.

Though Daniels led the final drive, it was the defense that kept the Commanders around all night. It held the NFL's hottest offense to only 20 points and continued its improved play.

With a game next week against Arizona, the Commanders have a chance to get to .500.

Here are the most important things to know for both teams:

Washington Commanders (4-5-1) 

Trend to watch: Running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt returned from a groin injury and provided a boost. He carried the ball 13 times for 54 yards and caught two passes for 23 yards. In his previous outing before getting hurt, he gained 82 yards on 11 carries. 

Most surprising performance: Washington's defense was outstanding. Joe Burrow entered having completed 21 of his last 22 passes vs. the blitz, but the Commanders never shied from that tactic: He was 8-of-16 for 59 yards Monday. They also limited receivers Tee Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase, holding them to a combined seven catches for 74 yards and a touchdown.

What to make of the QB performance: Jayden Daniels is getting more and more comfortable. The QB showed his dynamic ability on a 47-yard run. He finished with 289 yards passing and 55 rushing. He kept his eyes upfield on a 29-yard pass off a scramble. Daniels overcame a sluggish start with 85 yards passing at halftime. -- John Keim

Next game: Sunday at Arizona Cardinals, 4:25 p.m. ET, Fox

Cincinnati Bengals (7-3) 

Things looked promising for Cincinnati early on Monday night.

But the momentum the Bengals built, both in the game and during a five-game winning streak, was halted in a loss to the Commanders.

Cincinnati was ineffective on both sides of the ball in the second half. Washington scored on six straight drives, including the game-winning field goal as time expired. The Bengals' offense stalled out late in the contest and couldn't curb the Commanders' surge at Northwest Stadium. 

Trend to watch: Bengals edge rusher Boye Mafe has been on a roll recently. He had three sacks in the first half alone, making him the first player this season to achieve that feat. Mafe has had a sack in six of his past seven games.

articles.headline: Jayden Daniels rallies Commanders in final seconds to set up winning kick in 22-20 win over Bengals
articles.description: — Jayden Daniels connected with rookie Antonio Williams on two long pass plays, moving the Commanders 64 yards in 34 seconds to set up Drew Stevens’
articles.body:
LANDOVER, Md. -- — Jayden Daniels connected with rookie Antonio Williams on two long pass plays, moving the Commanders 64 yards in 34 seconds to set up Drew Stevens’ 26-yard field goal as time expired, and the Washington Commanders stunned Joe Burrow and the Cincinnati Bengals 22-20 on Monday night.


              After Evan McPherson put the Bengals ahead 20-19 on a 56-yard field goal, Washington got the ball back with 39 seconds left and no timeouts. Daniels hit Williams over the middle for 22 yards, spiked the ball, then found him again for a 42-yard catch-and-run to the Cincinnati 8. The QB spiked it with 5 seconds left and Stevens did the rest.


              Daniels finished with 283 yards passing, Williams had nine catches for 122 yards, and Stevens was 5 for 5 on field goals as Washington (4-5-1) remained in the NFC East race, two games behind the division-leading New York Giants.


              Burrow threw for 300 yards and two touchdowns for AFC North-leading Cincinnati (7-3), but the Commanders largely held in check a Bengals team that had won five straight, scoring 31 points or more each time. Washington's defense forced Burrow to settle for checkdowns all night.


              The dangerous Bengals receiving duo of Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins combined for just seven catches for 74 yards.


              Washington coach Dan Quinn made another questionable late-game decision when he sent Stevens out on fourth-and-1 to kick a 41-yard field goal with 2:26 left for a 19-17 lead. That left plenty of time for Burrow, who found Mike Gesicki for a 32-yard completion to move the Bengals into field goal range.


              A sack pushed the Bengals back, but McPherson nailed the long kick with 46 seconds remaining.


              The game got off to a slow start in rainy conditions but opened up in the second half as the teams traded scores throughout the third quarter. Burrow's 4-yard touchdown pass to Colbie Young put the Bengals ahead 17-10, and the Commanders rallied with three field goals by Stevens.


              There was an unexpected stoppage early in the third when the stadium lights went out with the Commanders in the red zone. After a delay that lasted about four minutes, Stevens converted from 36 yards to tie the game at 10-all.


              Washington held Cincinnati to three points on its first four drives before Higgins' 31-yard touchdown catch that made it 10-0. Jacory Croskey-Merritt, activated off injured reserve earlier Monday, scored on a 1-yard run for the Commanders with 12 seconds left before halftime.


              Injuries
              Bengals: Safety Bryan Cook suffered a right ankle injury but returned to the game.


              Up next
              Bengals: Host the New Orleans Saints on Sunday.


              Commanders: Visit the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday.


              ------

articles.headline: Jalen Green scores 25 and Devin Booker adds 22 to help the Suns top the Pelicans 123-119 in OT
articles.description: — Jalen Green scored 25 points, Devin Booker added 22, and the Phoenix Suns defeated the New Orleans Pelicans, 123-119 in overtime on Monday night.
articles.body:
NEW ORLEANS -- — Jalen Green scored 25 points, Devin Booker added 22, and the Phoenix Suns defeated the New Orleans Pelicans, 123-119 in overtime on Monday night.


              Collin Gillespie scored five of his 18 points in overtime, and Miles Bridges had 13 points and 11 rebounds for Phoenix, which won its fourth straight game while handing New Orleans its fourth straight loss.


              Jordan Poole scored 28 points — all in the first three quarters — and Zion Williamson added 25 points for the Pelicans, who've dropped 10 of 11 since starting 4-4. 


              Saddiq Bey added 21 points and Jeremiah Fears had 11 assists for New Orleans. But Fears, who'd scored 29 points in a loss at San Antonio on Saturday, missed 14 of 17 shots against Phoenix. Trey Murphy also struggled as he works his way back from knee soreness that had sidelined him for seven of New Orleans' previous eight games. He shot 4 of 14 from the floor, and 1 of 6 from 3-point range. 


              The Suns pulled away for good with a 10-4 run during overtime that included Booker's jumper, Gillespie's layup as he was fouled and Bridges' 3.


              Phoenix also led 109-107 with 31 seconds left in regulation after Booker's step-back jumper. Fears' driving scoop tied it at 109 with 22.8 seconds left, and Herb Jones' steal of Booker's pass in the final seconds of the fourth quarter forced overtime.


              Poole, who scored 25 points two nights earlier in San Antonio, made his first nine shots against Phoenix, including six from 3-point range.


              He scored 17 in the first half, after which Phoenix led 56-54.


              Derik Queen scored 11 points for the Pelicans, but missed four of five free throws in the fourth quarter, when the Pelicans missed six of 12 from the line.


              Up next
              Suns: At Houston in NBA Cup West Group A play on Wednesday.


              Pelicans: At Los Angeles Clippers in NBA Cup West Group B play on Friday.

articles.headline: Kevin Durant scores 32 to power Rockets past Clippers 116-104
articles.description: — Kevin Durant scored 32 points and Alperen Sengun and Amen Thompson each had 20 to lead the Houston Rockets to a 116-104 win over the Los Angeles Clippers on Monday night.
articles.body:
HOUSTON -- — Kevin Durant scored 32 points and Alperen Sengun and Amen Thompson each had 20 to lead the Houston Rockets to a 116-104 win over the Los Angeles Clippers on Monday night.


              Houston led by six points with about three minutes remaining before Durant made consecutive 3-pointers to make it 109-97.


              Brandon Ingram made a basket for Los Angeles but an off-balance 3 by Durant seconds later put the Rockets up 112-99 with 1:30 remaining.


              Ingram made his debut with the Clippers after sitting out since May following surgery for a heel injury and to repair a partially torn Achilles tendon.


              The two-time All-Star joined the Clippers in September from Toronto as part of the trade for Kawhi Leonard. He missed the last two games of Toronto’s first-round playoff series against Cleveland because of the injury.


              He had 16 points and seven rebounds in 27 minutes.


              Darius Garland had 26 points and eight assists to lead the Clippers, who lost their fourth straight. Rui Hachimura added 19 points.


              The game was tied midway through the third quarter before the Rockets used a 9-0 run, capped by a 3 from Tari Eason, to make it 74-65. Houston led by 10 entering the fourth.


              Up next
              Clippers: Visit Memphis on Wednesday night.


              Rockets: Host Phoenix on Wednesday night.

articles.headline: Bulls beat Cavaliers 122-108 behind Jordan Hawkins' 19 points and 63 off the bench
articles.description: — Jordan Hawkins scored a season-high 19 points, Buddy Hield had 17 and the Chicago Bulls got 63 points off the bench as they held on to beat the Cleveland Cavaliers 122-108 on Monday night.
articles.body:
CHICAGO -- — Jordan Hawkins scored a season-high 19 points, Buddy Hield had 17 and the Chicago Bulls got 63 points off the bench as they held on to beat the Cleveland Cavaliers 122-108 on Monday night.


              Matas Buzelis added 15 points — all in the first half — as Bulls coach Tiago Splitter spread out playing time after a 151-145 overtime loss to Denver on Sunday. Tre Jones finished with 16 points and nine assists as six Bulls players reached double figures.


              Chicago shot 45.8% from the field and hit 20 of 49 from 3-point range. 


              Donovan Mitchell led the Cavs with 28 points and James Harden added 21 after the 37-year-old guard scored 51 in their previous game, a 128-119 win over Indiana on Friday.


              The Bulls put it away with a strong fourth quarter, including a 10-0 spurt capped by Josh Giddey's finger-roll layup 4:23 in that made it 113-97. Jones hit a quirky 3 with 3:56 to go to make it 120-104.


              Giddey was limited to four points, 11 assists and two rebounds in 22 minutes after posting 23 points, 14 rebounds and a career-high 22 assists on Sunday.


              Chicago was clinging to a 93-89 lead entering the fourth quarter after building a 24-point cushion with a big second quarter, when it outscored Cleveland 45-20. The Bulls led 72-50 at halftime.


              The score was tied 32-all a minute into the second period when the Bulls got hot — buoyed by their bench — while the Cavs went cold. Chicago opened the lead to 24 using a series of runs, including a 12-2 spurt.


              Chicago shot 49% in the half and hit 11 of 25 from long distance, with Buzelis nailing four 3s.


              The Cavs responded immediately in the third quarter, starting with a 9-0 run. They outscored Chicago 39-21 in the period to trim it to 93-89 on Mitchell's driving layup with 2 seconds left.


              Up next
              Cavaliers: At the New York Knicks on Wednesday.


              Bulls: At Charlotte on Wednesday.

articles.headline: Seahawks to monitor Sam Darnold status this week before final call vs. 49ers
articles.description: The Seahawks still plan to start Sam Darnold against the 49ers but will wait to see how the QB looks in practice Wednesday before making a final call.
articles.body:
RENTON, Wash. -- The Seattle Seahawks still plan to start Sam Darnold against the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday but will wait to see how the quarterback looks in practice Wednesday before making a final decision, coach Mike Macdonald said.

Darnold has missed the past two games because of a quad injury he suffered near the end of Seattle's loss to the Chicago Bears in Week 8, when he also suffered a cracked rib on his first dropback of the night. Macdonald said last Monday that Darnold would start this week as long as he made the progress over the bye that the team was projecting.

Speaking with reporters Monday, Macdonald said the quarterback made "a good bit of progress."

"He was able to train a little bit here, do some rehab here," Macdonald said. "He also was able to get away. He's optimistic, but I think just with today's practice cadence and speed today, I think it's probably wise to wait to make any declarations until we get through Wednesday's practice."

The Seahawks held a bonus practice Monday coming off their bye. They were not required to release an injury report, but Darnold -- who had not practiced since the Nov. 2 Bears game -- was seen jogging out for warmups with his helmet on, and Macdonald confirmed that he took part.

"He looked great," the coach said. "Everything was positive today. He took a ton of reps, but it wasn't a full-speed -- it was more of a [walk-through] tempo."

With the first-place 49ers (9-1) winning Sunday night, the reigning Super Bowl champion Seahawks (6-4) are now three games back in the NFC West standings heading into Sunday's game at Levi's Stadium. San Francisco won the first meeting at Lumen Field in October.

Darnold's quad and rib injuries were the latest setbacks in what has been a trying start to the season. He injured his glute on the fifth play of the opener, missing the remainder of that game and the following week. In six full games, he has thrown 10 touchdown passes and nine interceptions.

Backup Drew Lock, meanwhile, has thrown seven touchdown passes with zero interceptions over the four games in which he has filled in -- all Seattle victories. Lock has been dealing with a right elbow injury for over a month, and he also played through an oblique injury last week while quarterbacking Seattle to a win over the Las Vegas Raiders.

"I'd say the bye week was really helpful for Drew," Macdonald said. "I think a well-deserved chance for him to feel better, and that's going to help us moving forward. But I think that's the case for several of our guys as well."

Macdonald did not have injury updates on any other players Monday. Defensive tackle Leonard Williams missed the past two games with a stinger that kept him out of practice both weeks. He was on the field for warmups Monday with his helmet.

articles.headline: David Moyes accepts James Tarkowski red card in Everton defeat to Brentford
articles.description: Everton manager David Moyes said he understood why James Tarkowski was shown a straight red card in the 4-0 defeat to Brentford.
articles.body:
LONDON -- Everton manager David Moyes said he understood why James Tarkowski was shown a straight red card in the 4-0 defeat to Brentford despite initially thinking it was the incorrect decision.

The Everton captain was penalised for a tackle on Yegor Yarmolyuk in the 40th minute, where he got the ball but caught the Brentford midfielder high up on the shin with his follow through.

Referee Craig Pawson had initially shown Tarkowski a yellow card, but he was forced to reconsider his decision by VAR and subsequently upgraded it to a red card.

Everton were already 2-0 down by this point courtesy of a Keane Lewis-Potter brace and the red card dented any chances they had of producing a comeback. Second-half goals from Vitaly Janelt and Fábio Carvalho added to Everton's misery and saw them fall to ninth in the Premier League.

"My first feeling at the time was I didn't think it was red because I thought James easily got to the ball before. He easily got to the ball before the Brentford player, so I would have said that the Brentford player was a bit late in getting there," Moyes said in his post-match news conference.

"But obviously after I've seen it again, I've seen Tarki's boots are a bit higher so I can understand why the position went against us."

Unsurprisingly, Brentford boss Keith Andrews was also in agreement with the decision to send off Tarkowski.

"I don't think he can tackle like that in this day and age. We've also been on the wrong side of some decisions in recent weeks that have cost us. So I'm certainly not going to challenge that one," Andrews said.

The 4-0 win over Everton pushes Brentford into sixth place and puts them in firm contention for a Champions League spot. In the previous two years, the top five teams have qualified for Europe's elite competition.

Brentford have never qualified for any tier of European football, missing out on the Conference League last year due to goal difference.

- Vitaly Janelt hits stunner as Brentford stroll to victory over 10-man Everton

- Man United to appeal Leny Yoro red card against Liverpool - sources

- Kevin De Bruyne: Man City achievements will not be tainted if appeal fails

When asked if European qualification was the primary target this season, Andrews said: "We're just doing what we do. I think we set out this season looking to be better than last season. I think if that happens, naturally we might be flying to different destinations next year.

"So we've got a very competitive squad. We've got an amazing group of young men that want to strive and want to get better. I think if we continue with that mindset, we'll hopefully be in a good place."

Everton host Liverpool in the Merseyside derby on Sunday, while Brentford travel to Manchester United the day before.

articles.headline: Vitaly Janelt hits stunner as Brentford stroll to victory over 10-man Everton
articles.description: Vitaly Janelt scored a 30-yard screamer as Brentford romped to a 4-0 victory against 10-man Everton at the Gtech Community Stadium.
articles.body:
Vitaly Janelt scored a 30-yard screamer as Brentford romped to a 4-0 victory against 10-man Everton at the Gtech Community Stadium.

One win in five had seen some of the early season optimism around Keith Andrews' team fade but this was an emphatic response to fire them up the Premier League table to sixth, even if culpability for Everton's collapse lay largely with James Tarkowski, red carded in the 40th minute for a horror tackle on Yegor Yarmolyuk.

David Moyes was setting a new record for number of games in charge of Everton, this his 593rd match eclipsing the tally Harry Catterick racked up during the 60s and 70s, but this was a terrible first half and was no way to mark such an achievement.

Everything went wrong for the visitors. Both Brentford goals scored by Keane Lewis-Potter came via deflections and Tarkowski's momentary abdication of responsibility as captain, lunging studs-up into the shin of Yarmolyuk with his team 2-0 down, would have been impossible for Moyes to mitigate. He was let down badly by one of his senior players in a moment of direst need.

Thereafter the game was little contest. It might have trickled towards a routine two-goal win for Brentford had Janelt not pulled out a brilliant strike from range that ripped past Jordan Pickford to rub salt in the wound for Moyes, and for Tarkowski.

Fábio Carvalho bundled one in from on the goalline with his knee in stoppage time, the final indignity for Everton.

Brentford were excellent throughout. Early on, Callum Wilson fed Michael Kayode arriving up on the right, the full-back given a clear shot on Pickford's goal but dragging his effort badly across the face and wide.

Everton were making it too easy. Midway through the half they failed to deal with a ball over the top and Jaidon Anthony sent it low into the middle with a deft stab of the toe. It was a beautifully controlled first-time pass, finding Lewis-Potter arriving in an acre of space and his shot spun in off the lunging Jarrad Branthwaite.

It took less than two minutes for Lewis-Potter to hit a near-identical second, with a ball into the box from Mikkel Damsgaard met with unconvincing Everton defending.

The Brentford midfielder was given two attempts, his first shot rebounding back to him to squeeze the ball in at the second go via a deflection off Thierno Barry.

Everton were sinking and their captain abandoned them to their fate. Tarkowski was first shown only a yellow for a studs-up challenge on Yarmolyuk. A single look at a replay confirmed the foul was far more serious, the defender's boot connecting high on the shin of Yarmolyuk's standing leg and his dismissal was inevitable.

Jack Grealish came on to try to raise Everton, his first appearance after five games absent for disciplinary matters.

articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Manchester United eye move for Ivan Toney
articles.description: Manchester United are looking to improve their attack by signing Al Ahli's Ivan Toney. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.body:
Manchester United are interested signing in Al Ahli striker Ivan Toney, while Liverpool defender Virgil van Dijk could move to AC Milan on a free transfer in the summer. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Manchester United are interested signing in Al Ahli striker Ivan Toney, TEAMtalk reports. The Red Devils have asked to be kept updated on the 30-year-old's situation, as his representatives are in discussions with multiple clubs regarding a switch in January. The England international is keen to return to Europe and could move on a loan that would include an option to be made permanent. He has also been linked with Crystal Palace.

- AC Milan are monitoring the situation of Liverpool defender Virgil van Dijk, with plans to reinforce their defense in the next two transfer windows, according to Tuttosport. The 35-year-old is reported to be eyeing a spell in Italy, and enters the final six months of his contract in January, but Corriere dello Sport reports that Milan are also tracking Sporting CP defender Gonçalo Inácio. Furthermore, the club have made Real Madrid striker Endrick their No. 1 priority, according to Gazzetta dello Sport, and see the 20-year-old as a better fit for their squad than Club Brugge's Nicolo Tresoldi. Milan are hopeful of using their strong relationship with Los Blancos to explore a loan or permanent signing that would involve a clause which allows the LaLiga side to bring him back to the Bernabéu in the future.

- Barcelona are facing competition from Chelsea, Manchester United and Manchester City for the signing of FC Twente defender Ruud Nijstad, according to Diario Sport. The Blaugrana have been at the front of the queue for the 18-year-old, but there are concerns they may not be able to secure a move for him in January due to the Eredivisie club demanding a fee worth in excess of €20 million, and Premier League sides are now emerging as suitors.

- Arsenal are interested in RB Leipzig winger Antonio Nusa, Football Insider reports. The 21-year-old has been identified as a long-term option by the Gunners, but would require the Bundesliga club to lower their €66 million valuation for a deal to become possible in the January transfer window. Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta is continuing to assess options to reinforce his side's left flank, while Nusa would be keen on a switch to the Emirates.

- Juventus remain admirers of Manchester United forward Joshua Zirkzee, with manager Luciano Spalletti hopeful of adding a "physical striker" to his team in January, according to Calciomercato. Zirkzee, 25, is seen as an ideal fit for the Bianconeri's style of play, and he is one of the preferred options of club chief football officer Frederic Massara. articles.headline: Kevin De Bruyne: Man City achievements will not be tainted if appeal fails
articles.description: Kevin De Bruyne insists his achievements will not be tainted if Manchester City are stripped of any titles.
articles.body:
Kevin De Bruyne insists his achievements will not be tainted if Manchester City are stripped of any titles.

De Bruyne won a host of honours, including six Premier League crowns and the Champions League, during a glorious 10-year spell at City that ended when he joined Napoli in 2025.

A shadow has since been cast over City's most successful era after the club were found guilty of serious breaches of the Premier League's financial regulations in September.

Among the punishments City could face if they fail in an appeal is the removing of some of their honours.

De Bruyne, 35, said he remains proud of the part he played in those triumphs and retains huge affection for the club's owners.

De Bruyne, who is back at the Etihad Stadium as Napoli face City in the Champions League on Tuesday, said at a news conference: "I'm proud of what I've done as a football player, and honestly, this is my club, I love the owners.

"I've even spoken to [chairman] Khaldoon [Al Mubarak] about how to buy a club.

"I have nothing but affection for this club, and that will never change, [the way] the people treated me and my family for 10 years.

"Of course, in life there are rules, but everybody plays on the limit. I played in between the white lines, and I competed with other players, and I had many experiences with my teams, with the players. That's the thing that I value most.

"I've given my all and that's not going to change in my mind. I don't think a lot of people will change in their mind how they view me as a player, or how we played.

"But everybody has their own opinion, I guess. Other people may be 'disgraced' a bit, but I can't change anything about that."

De Bruyne's return to Manchester comes amid reports he is unsettled at Napoli and could seek a move in January.

He did not address his future or speculation about tensions with coach Massimiliano Allegri and some teammates, but he did express frustration at the media reaction to comments by his wife about life in Naples.

- Maresca calls Man City's league slump 'a shame' before De Bruyne reunion

- Champions League Power Rankings before MD5: Who's No. 1?

- Enzo Maresca: Man City denied 'clear' goal in draw with Fulham

He said: "To be honest, I am pretty annoyed. A lot of noise came and a lot of bad reactions to my wife and family. I saw pictures of my house -- I don't think it is OK.

"But it is what it is. Some press created this in Italy, I don't know why. Nobody knows my life, you will never know. It has not been nice for my wife, for my family."

Asked about De Bruyne's future, Allegri said: "As far as Kevin is concerned, we have not spoken about that because at the moment we are caught up in all of these games.

"Over Christmas there will be a short break then the transfer window will open and the club will be open to try and bring in reinforcements. Then it is down to the players and who wants to leave."

articles.headline: Champions League Power Rankings before MD5: Who's No. 1?
articles.description: The UEFA Champions League is going at full speed, and we're beyond the halfway point of the league phase. Injuries are starting to pile up. Where does your club rank?
articles.body:
We're officially past the midway point of the UEFA Champions League league phase as the 2026-27 European season rumbles on, and the grind of the calendar is beginning to take its toll on the elite teams, with injuries starting to pile up. Harry Kane (Bayern Munich), Désiré Doué (Paris Saint-Germain) and David Raya (Arsenal) were all sidelined this weekend with issues of varying severity, and it's only going to get more grueling as we head toward the hectic festive period and, beyond that, the January transfer window.

So what has it done to the standings? Throughout the competition, we will be asking our writers, editors and other experts to rank the top 10 teams in the tournament in terms of who they think are the strongest and most likely to win it all. Here are your Champions League Power Rankings going into a fun week.

UCL Power Rankings before Matchday 5

1. PARIS SAINT-GERMAIN (no change)

- Previous rank: 1

- Games since MD3: defeated Lyon 2-0; defeated Le Havre 5-1; defeated Villarreal 6-0; defeated Troyes 1-0; defeated Nice 3-2

- MD5 opponent: vs. AS Roma (Wednesday)

Would anyone bet against them winning it all a third straight time? Our voters were nearly unanimous -- 15 of 17 -- in crowning the French champions and back-to-back Champions League winners as the best team in this competition, but there are tough tests to come.

PSG continue to look sharp and ruthless domestically, which isn't normally their rhythm at this time of year. (Folks will remember that they generally wake up, form-wise, after Christmas, at least in recent seasons.) Ferran Torres keeps showing why he was such a savvy summer signing from Barcelona, chipping in eight goals and an assist as an occasional starter, with the likes of Senny Mayulu -- one of 12 players to get on the score sheet in Ligue 1 this season -- also stepping up to contribute in the attacking third.

They were managing without Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, who tore his ACL in October and faces a lengthy spell on the sideline, but Saturday's season-ending knee injury suffered by Doué in this weekend's win over Nice will tax their reserves over the course of a grueling campaign. Up next is a potentially tricky midweek date with Roma who, despite losing to Man United in Matchday 4, have one of the stingiest defenses in Serie A (11 goals conceded in 12 games).

2. BARCELONA (no change)

- Previous rank: 2

- Games since MD3: lost 2-1 vs. Real Madrid; defeated Alaves 6-1; defeated Aston Villa 3-0; defeated Atletico Madrid 2-1; defeated Villarreal 3-2

- MD5 opponent: at Sabah FK (Wednesday)

The Spanish champions continue to be box-office entertainment every week. They simply do not believe in drawing games; every single one of their games this season has ended with a decisive winner and loser, with their back-to-back losses to PSG and Real Madrid surrounded by wins up and down the schedule. articles.headline: Oli McBurnie is Hull's 'Braveheart,' says Sergej Jakirovic after Brighton win
articles.description: Hull manager Sergej Jakirovic has likened striker Oli McBurnie to Scottish warrior William Wallace, as depicted by Mel Gibson in the 1995 film Braveheart.
articles.body:
Hull manager Sergej Jakirovic has likened striker Oli McBurnie to Scottish warrior William Wallace, as depicted by Mel Gibson in the 1995 film Braveheart.

McBurnie scored two goals in stoppage time as Hull shocked high-flying Brighton 2-0 at home on Sunday.

McBurnie's resurgence has also seen him recalled to the Scotland squad, and Jakirovic was not shy in his praise for the 30-year-old.

He named him as a crucial member of his team, with Regan Slater, Lewie Coyle, Matt Crooks and John Egan also credited for the roles they are playing at the club.

"It is normal to him, he's in the Scottish national team. He is Braveheart, like the movie," Jakirovic said of McBurnie's late goals and never-say-die attitude.

"He's excellent, there is no doubt about Oli, ever. I never have any doubt about Oli McBurnie because he is a natural leader.

"He doesn't need telling, he is leading the team together with Slater, Coyle and Crooksy -- John Egan is there too.

"They are very, very important to us."
